newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bank debentures weaken on LDP official's remarks.
newsitem.headline: Bank debentures weaken on LDP official's remarks.

text.p: Five-year debentures issued by Japanese banks came under selling pressure in Tokyo on Monday after a ruling party official said debentures bought by institutional investors should not be protected with public funds, bond traders said.

Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, said in a television programme on Sunday that bank debentures sold to institutional investors should not be protected by use of public funds.

A 1.6 percent five-year debenture issued in March by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) was tagged with a bid quote of 1.75 percent on Monday morning. It was traded at a yield of 1.65 percent on Friday.
Meanwhile, five-year IBJ debentures issued in January and February with the same coupon were traded at around 1.72 and 1.73 percent, respectively, on Monday morning, traders said.
